properties.name: Azinha
properties.flight_rules:
Most of the flying area is under the Temporary Reserved Airspace areas TRA54 and TRA55, used mainly for military purpose.
The normal maximum altitude allowed is 3200m (10500 feet), but often for events in the area, NOTAMs to FL125 (3810m or 12500 feet).
properties.going_there: 11km of Tarmac road from LZ plus 3 km more of dirt road (about 20minutea)
properties.comments:
Azinha is the cornerstone of the flying sites in Serra da Estrela. With its South facing take-off high above the valley it presents a stunning view towards Torre (the highest peak of Serra da Estrela mountain ridge and continental Portugal) and over the the river ZÃªzere.
(©clubevertical.org)
properties.weather:
Flight conditions: Due to the South exposure, with the Sun heating the slope, and the orographic characteristics of the spot, it is possible to fly with any wind direction, if the meteorological wind speed does not exceed 15km/h. If the meteorological wind is also south then it should be limited to 20km/h, with the thermal activity adding up to it, it normally works all day. East wind works until 18h and North and West wind until 15h. Ideal forecast is a light south or westerly wind.
(©clubevertical.org)

properties.name: Castelo de Vide
properties.takeoff_description:
Medium large gravel field, ok for simultaneous preparation for >5 gliders, with a medium small slope.
Currently there is no windsock (as of January 2025)
The takeoff is accessible by a short gravel road connecting to the asphalted panoramic road, no need for 4x4 drive.
From the landing the takeoff can be hiked back in max 30 minutes - initially on the small access road, and then "straight up" once on the hill below the take-off location.
properties.flight_rules: Check the airspace and NOTAMS on: https://cavok.pt/fuaflex/fua-portugal/
properties.going_there: Accessible for public by small gravel road (see maps). There is an roadsign on the asphalted road pointing at the takeoff.
properties.comments: Possibly good for soaring in winter, and with high XC potential in summer with W or SW wind, although in summer the wind from NE is dominating.
properties.weather: SW wind is the best.

landing.landing_description:
There are multiple large grass fields below right in front of the take-off. Note sure any of them is an official landing site. The largest field is surrounded by a barber wire. The smaller field on the left (where the landing position on the map is) has got an exit without a need to climb over the fence.
A common sense would be landing on a spot where there is no livestock..

no high voltage cables, no trees, and wide wind range to take off without obstacles and no cloudbase below, easy toplanding, a dream for pilots!

!!! REGARDING FLYING ON THE NORTH COAST !!!

Please take in consideration the following before attempting to fly on the north coast:
 
- Safe landing zones are very scarce, they are often very short, narrow and rocky.
- High tide levels can make them even shorter or completely disappear.
-The cloud base tends to form at low altitude, if youâ€™re flying and it happens below your flight level it can be disorientating
- The sea state ranges from moderate, 1.25 to 2.5 meters wave height, to very rought, 4 to 6 meters wave height. In the event of landing in the water it will be extremely difficult to reach the shore.
- Especially with lower pressure, wind speed and direction can change and consequently its effects on the sharp edges and abrupt orography of the coast can originate dangerous rotors and whirls.
 
We strongly advice all pilots, regardless of their level of experience, to contact AVLM before attempting to fly on the north coast to double check the weather conditions.

properties.name: Marvão
properties.takeoff_description:
The takeoff is just below the village's defence wall - a grassy field, with a sort of "ramp", which may be convenient for a hang glider launch. The access to the takeoff from the village is through a small metal gate just above the takeoff. The gate normally is not locked. If locked, one has to walk around and climb to the takeoff from below.
The takeoff itself is slightly "technical" due to the rotor from the edge, not for the beginners.
properties.flight_rules:
Check airspace and NOTAMs on https://cavok.pt/fuaflex/fua-portugal/
The landing is not an official landing, so please be very respectful!
properties.going_there: The takeoff can be accessed from the Marvao village.
properties.comments:
Flying over Marvao village and the castle is very beautiful.
In good conditions, one can turn the thermal and fly an XC to Spain.
properties.weather: The best soaring is when there is a 15-20kmh wind from SW.

landing.landing_description:
Technically the best option is the large grass field just in front of the takeoff. It is surrounded by a fence, which is quite low at few places (near the parking at landing) and can be easily climbed over. Since it is not an official landing, a common sense would be not landing there if livestock is present. Also, after the landing, leave the field and then fold the wing in one of the parkings around.
In alternative, there are other fields further ahead, including golf course, and a rather large car parking, which is typically empty in low season.
